definitions.explanation: Used after verbs, adjectives, or nouns to create temporal clauses meaning 'when' or 'at the time of.' Functions as a dependent noun that describes the timing of the main clause.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}に{行|い}った{時|とき}、{富士山|ふじさん}を{見|み}ました。
examples.english: When I went to Japan, I saw Mt. Fuji.

examples.japanese: {暇|ひま}な{時|とき}に{来|き}てください。
examples.english: Please come when you have free time.

examples.japanese: {困|こま}った{時|とき}は{連絡|れんらく}してください。
examples.english: When you're in trouble, please contact me.

examples.japanese: {分|わ}からない{時|とき}は{先生|せんせい}に{聞|き}いてください。{何度|なんど}{聞|き}いても{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です。
examples.english: When you don't understand, please ask the teacher. It's fine to ask as many times as you want.

examples.japanese: {買|か}い{物|もの}をする{時|とき}は、いつも{値段|ねだん}を{比|くら}べてから{買|か}うようにしている。
examples.english: When I go shopping, I always try to compare prices before buying.

notes:
GRAMMAR PATTERNS:
- Verb (plain) + {時|とき}: {食|た}べる{時|とき} (when eating)
- Verb (た form) + {時|とき}: {食|た}べた{時|とき} (when [I] ate)
- い-adjective + {時|とき}: {若|わか}い{時|とき} (when young)
- な-adjective + な + {時|とき}: {暇|ひま}な{時|とき} (when free)
- Noun + の + {時|とき}: {子供|こども}の{時|とき} (when [I was] a child)

TENSE NUANCE:
- {行|い}く{時|とき} = when going (before/during)
- {行|い}った{時|とき} = when [I] went (completed action)

This tense distinction is important: dictionary form emphasizes the time before or during the action, while た form emphasizes after the action is complete.

Often followed by particles like は or に: {時|とき}は (when..., as for), {時|とき}に (at the time when).
